name: Orkes: LLM Task Fails Because llmProvider Is a Provider Type, Not an Integration Name
query: My summarize_ticket workflow works on my local Conductor but on our Orkes cluster the LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE task fails saying the integration 'anthropic' was not found. The task has llmProvider: "anthropic" and model: "claude-sonnet-4-6". Our admins say Anthropic is configured. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Explain that on Orkes `llmProvider` is the name of an integration configured on the cluster, not the provider type — locally (OSS) `anthropic` is the provider name, so the same JSON works there

Step 2: List the AI integrations this application can see: `python3 "$CONDUCTOR_API" integration-list --category AI_MODEL`, and note the list only shows integrations shared with this application — the admins' integration may exist but not be shared
Step 3: If it is visible, check the model with `model-list --provider <name>`; if `claude-sonnet-4-6` is missing, add it with `model-save`, and on 403 have the user (or admins) add it in the UI

Step 4: If it is not visible, have the integration shared with the running application in the UI (Access Control → Applications → <app> → Integration tab), or ask the admins for its name; confirm with `integration-wait --type anthropic --model claude-sonnet-4-6`
Step 5: Update `llmProvider` to the integration name, write the workflow to a file, `conductor workflow update`, and re-run to verify
success_criteria: Identifies the cause: on Orkes `llmProvider` must be the integration NAME configured on the cluster, which differs from the provider type that works on OSS

Lists the AI integrations (`integration-list` or `GET /api/integrations/provider`) to find the real name rather than guessing, and explains an empty or partial list can mean the integration isn't shared with this application
Checks the model is registered under that integration (`model-list`), adding it with `model-save` or via the UI when the save is forbidden
Mentions sharing the integration with the running application (UI Access Control → Applications → Integration tab) and verifying (`integration-wait` or `access-list`)
Fixes the workflow by changing `llmProvider` to the integration name, writing the JSON to a file and updating/re-running it

Does not create a second Anthropic integration, does not ask for the Anthropic key in chat, does not suggest an HTTP call to api.anthropic.com, and does not tell the user to set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on the Orkes server as the fix
